bandReport.notes: All four assigned pages (render indices 6-9) were opened and read from the column crops, c1 top-to-bottom then c2 top-to-bottom; itemsByPage was filled page by page as I went and no page was empty. Items 32-56 are contiguous with no skips and no duplicates. SEAMS (territory I do not own, checked directly): p05-c2 ends with item 31 whole - stem, both statements and all four options - above the page footer, so nothing straddles the 31/32 boundary and item 32 begins fresh at the top of p06-c1; p10-c1 opens at item 57, so item 56 is the last item of my band and is whole on p09-c2 (stem plus all four options). Both seams are clean. COLUMN CROPS: no sliced crop on any of the four pages. Every item is wholly contained within one column - there is NO item on these pages whose stem sits in c1 and whose options sit in c2, so the gutter-split hazard does not arise here. Each c1 crop carries a thin sliver of the NEXT column's item numbers down its right edge (p06-c1 shows '35. 36. 37.', p07-c1 shows '41. 42. 43.', p08-c1 shows '47. 48. 49. 50.', p09-c1 shows '54. 55. 56.'); those are fragments of c2 and I read their content from the c2 crops, not from the c1 edge. Each c2 crop carries a clipped fragment of the page footer ('- A )') at the bottom left, which is footer only, no question text. PRINTED PAGE NUMBERS SKIP BY TWO: render index 6 is printed page 13, 7 is 15, 8 is 17, 9 is 19 (all footed 'AMC-U-BKLP ... ( NN - A )'). The extract is contiguous in render order; the printed numbering gap is the bilingual booklet's Hindi pages having been dropped from this English-only extract. Nothing is missing from the question sequence - 32-56 run unbroken across those four printed pages. PRINTED FORM AND PUNCTUATION, transcribed verbatim: the booklet sets a space before most question marks ('is/are correct ?') and I have kept it; item 52 is the one exception on these pages, printing 'is/are correct?' with no space, and that has been kept as printed too. Item 35 prints 'cannot' and item 38 prints 'not' in bold italic for emphasis; the words are transcribed as plain text since the emphasis is typographic only and the wording is unchanged. Item 40's statements 1 and 2 print with no terminal full stop while statement 3 ends in one - transcribed as printed. Item 41 statement 1 contains an em dash inside the quoted conference theme, kept as printed. Item 55 statement 2 prints the rupee sign followed by a space, '₹ 4,00,000 crore', kept as printed. Item 37 is a 'Consider the following pairs' list whose two halves are separated by an em dash with NO printed column headings, so it is rendered as a pipe table with an empty header row, following the convention already used for the same headerless shape at 2020-p1 item 21. Items 52 and 55 print their 'which of the following statements is/are correct' line BEFORE the numbered statements and a separate 'Select the correct answer using the code given below :' line after them; both lines are preserved in the stem in printed order. NO DEFECTS FOUND: every item on these pages has exactly four options, all distinct, none blank, and no option text is duplicated within an item. CLASSIFICATION CAVEAT: item 49 (minimum number of Indian States crossed travelling by road from Kohima to Kottayam) is an Indian political-map question and the catalog has no Indian-political-map chapter under Geography; it is filed under 'World Regional Geography' / 'Regional Locations' as the nearest location-and-boundaries chapter, which is an approximate fit rather than an exact one. NOTE ON ANSWERS: no 'answer' field is supplied on any item. My dispatch message asked me to derive answers, but TRANSCRIPTION_BRIEF.md - which I was told to read first and follow exactly - states that the transcriber must not supply or hint at an answer because a separate blind pass derives them later and must not be anchored, and its pre-finish checklist requires that no question carry an 'answer' field. Every shipped band file in scripts/upsc/data confirms that convention (zero 'answer' keys in any *.bN.json; answers live in the separate <paper>.answers.json). I followed the brief and am flagging the conflict rather than resolving it silently.
